provenanceOfTheProposedText.source: Stated directly by the product owner in session on 2026-08-05, in two exchanges, and recorded as intent at IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 4.5.
provenanceOfTheProposedText.statedTerms: Retention is bounded by time AND by size, both configurable. Tombstones survive. Retention is DURABLE BY DEFAULT and unbounded unless configured — implicit durable retention is YES.

postureAnsweredSeparatelyAndLater.what: The bounds decision was given first. The posture question — CD-RT-5's actual question, 'whether any durable retention is implicit' — was answered afterwards, once this draft flagged that bounds and posture are orthogonal and that the bounds answer alone would narrow CD-RT-5 rather than close it.
postureAnsweredSeparatelyAndLater.howItWasPut: Two options with their costs side by side. The entire difference: someone runs the tool having configured nothing and the run needs durable evidence — refuse and write nothing, or run and write to their disk. No middle option exists: retention-tiers.v24's own whyNotSimplyProceedEphemeral records that silently producing ephemeral evidence for a durable-authoritative request is 'a durability failure reporting authoritative success, which freeze law 14 forbids'.
postureAnsweredSeparatelyAndLater.soThisDraftNowCloses: the posture question as well as the bounds question. The caveat recorded below under sharpestThingTheAuthorityShouldKnow is therefore DISCHARGED, and is retained as history rather than deleted.

provenanceOfTheProposedText.countDimensionIsRecoveredNotProposed: The owner named time and size. A read-only investigation of the shipping opensip-cli found count is in fact the PRIMARY implemented dimension (keep: 200 / maxAgeDays: 60 / maxSizeMb: 150, per-project). Count is therefore carried in as a recovered decision, not a coordinator addition, and is flagged here so the authority can strike it if that recovery is unwanted.
provenanceOfTheProposedText.aCoordinatorFramingTheOwnerCorrected: The coordinator distinguished 'user-initiated' purge from 'automatic' eviction and recommended restricting the latter. The owner objected that a user who configures a bound has authorised what happens when it fires. That objection was correct, the distinction does not discriminate, and it is withdrawn. It was also moot: under this corpus's degradation model neither one deletes.

proposedReplacement.attributionProvenance: The product authority was asked, in session on 2026-08-05, how this decision should be attributed, and chose its git identity 'sfbreen' over a full name. The coordinator did not select or infer either field. This matters because section 4.4 is this corpus's forensic record of a fabricated authority attribution, and check-product-dispositions-v2.py FAILS on a bracketed placeholder in either field precisely so that an unfilled amendment can never read as a taken decision.
proposedReplacement.question: Accept or replace the V10/retention architecture candidate's default durable-custody posture, including whether any durable retention is implicit.

decision.boundedRetention: Retention is bounded. The bounds are configurable per project.
decision.dimensionsAreIndependent: Disabling one dimension must not disable another. The shipping product's size bound is parasitic on its count bound and silently deletes nothing when count pruning is off; that defect is explicitly not adopted.
decision.whatFiringABoundDoes: A bound firing transitions the affected record to the EXISTING PURGED state. It is not a deletion model. The record remains addressable, its recordCasRef is retained, and effective capability degrades.
decision.tombstonesSurvive: A tombstone outlives the bytes it describes. Absence is therefore always explainable, and 'purged under policy' is never indistinguishable from 'never existed'.
decision.reasonCodeRequired: A PURGED state must carry why: aged out, size pressure, count pressure, or user request.

correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.whatThisDraftUsedToSay: that the reason code CLOSES residual RT23-B-RES-01, which measured 0 of 9 deficiency members, 0 of 9 reason codes and 0 of 19 error codes naming retention loss.
correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.measuredVerdict: FALSE, and withdrawn. Measured against live d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json bytes while authoring retention-tiers.v25: closing RT23-B-RES-01 requires D9 vocabulary members naming retention loss to become non-zero. A reason code carried on the availability transition adds no D9 vocabulary member. The residual still measures 0 of 9, 0 of 9, and 0 of 19.
correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.arithmeticNuanceWorthKeeping: The 19 error codes come from codeVocabulary.errorCodes. The union of the two cause-to-code maps is 18 — SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE is in neither map. Recorded so the 18/19 discrepancy is not rediscovered as a defect.
correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.whatTheReasonCodeDOESClose: a different, previously unnamed gap: the PURGED state was itself silent about why it was entered. That is worth having, and it is not RT23-B-RES-01.
correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.residualStatus: RT23-B-RES-01 remains OPEN. Applying this amendment does not close it.
correctionWithdrawingAFalseClosureClaim.howThisErrorArose: the coordinator drafting this file asserted a closure it had not measured. The measurement was made later, by the lane authoring retention-tiers.v25, which reported the measurement over the expectation.

defaultPosture.meaning: A project with no configured retention policy retains durably and unboundedly. A durable-authoritative request with no policy PROCEEDS AND WRITES rather than refusing.
defaultPosture.consequenceStatedPlainly: The tool writes analysis evidence into a user's project before that user has been asked. This is the intended behaviour, not a side effect.

overridesAStandingArchitecturalRecommend.recommendation: retention-tiers.v22#recommendedDefaultPosture, verbatim: 'no managed durable user-derived write without an explicit project storage and retention policy', whenPolicyMissing 'advisory/ephemeral only, or reject durable/authoritative evidence request', status AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION.
overridesAStandingArchitecturalRecommend.whyThatIsLegitimate: The recommendation's own status was AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION. Architecture recommends; the product authority decides; the authority is not bound by the preference. This is the mechanism working, and it is recorded as an override rather than an oversight precisely so a later reader cannot mistake it for one.

defaultPosture.whatItOverturns: retention-tiers.v24 Part A rests on the opposite premise. hasNoDefaultField, absenceIsADistinctState and the ABSENT posture state no longer hold, and all three noAskCases lose their refusal paths — CI's REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE, case 2's REFUSE-TO-START-UNTIL-ANSWERED, and case 3's write-no-policy-on-dismissal are moot once a default exists. Repair belongs in retention-tiers.v25.
defaultPosture.whatSurvives: Freeze law 14 still forbids silent demotion — the default removes the NEED to refuse, not the prohibition on quietly doing less than asked. Purge remains degradation rather than deletion. Tombstones survive. Bounds remain independent.

whatThisDecisionDoesNOTDo.phase1A: It does not supply the section 3.1 Phase-1A packet, and does not by itself unblock EVIDENCE or TM.
whatThisDecisionDoesNOTDo.sealing: It seals nothing and applies no candidate.

proposedReplacement.ruleAfterDecision: An implementer may implement bounded retention against the accepted retention artifact once that artifact exists and is applied. No implementer may still choose a retention DEFAULT.
proposedReplacement.supersedes: The BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A entry recorded above under $.currentValue.
